zh.q: 太阳光为什么只能在南北回归线之间直射？
zh.concl: 因为黄赤交角 23°26′，地轴指向不变而地球在轨道上的位置在变，太阳光垂直照射的点只能在南北回归线之间往返，最北到北纬 23°26′、最南到南纬 23°26′。
points: 赤道平面与黄道平面之间的夹角叫黄赤交角，目前的黄赤交角是 23°26′。
地球在公转过程中，地轴的空间指向和黄赤交角的大小，在一定时期内可以看作是不变的。
所以太阳直射的范围最北到达北纬 23°26′、最南到达南纬 23°26′，这两条界线就叫北回归线、南回归线。

zh.q: 一年里，直射点怎样走完这一趟？
zh.concl: 直射点在南北回归线之间以一年为周期往返，叫太阳直射点的回归运动；这个周期就是一个回归年，二分二至是这条往返路线上的四个关键日期。
points: 夏至日（6 月 21 日前后）太阳直射北纬 23°26′，之后太阳直射点逐渐南移。
秋分日（9 月 23 日前后）直射赤道，冬至日（12 月 22 日前后）直射南纬 23°26′，之后逐渐北返。
直射点在南北回归线之间的往返运动，叫太阳直射点的回归运动；往返一次的周期是一个回归年。

zh.q: 北京的夏至正午，太阳升到多高？
zh.concl: 正午太阳高度 a = 90° − |φ − δ|：直射点上 90°、晨昏线上 0°，其余地方按与直射点的纬度差递减；北京 40°N 夏至 73°26′、冬至 26°34′。
points: 太阳高度是太阳光线与地平面的交角；在太阳直射点上，太阳高度是 90°。
正午太阳高度是一日内最大的太阳高度，反映太阳辐射的强弱。
正午太阳高度可以按 a = 90° − |φ − δ| 计算，δ 在夏半年取正值、冬半年取负值；北京（40°N）夏至 73°26′、冬至 26°34′。球上北京那块小板与水平光线之间的角就是 a；上方放大件把这块地面放平来看，弧旁的数随日期变。

zh.q: 同一天，为什么越往北太阳越低？
zh.concl: 就纬度分布而言，正午太阳高度夏至日由北回归线向南北两方降低，春分日和秋分日由赤道向两方降低，冬至日由南回归线向两方降低。
points: 同一天，离直射点纬度越远，正午太阳高度越小。
所以曲线（和真实的地球）最高处永远在直射点那条纬线上，它随日期南北移动。
夏至的峰值在北回归线，冬至在南回归线，春分日和秋分日在赤道。

zh.q: 本地正午太阳高度的最高值和最低值，什么时候出现？
zh.concl: 北回归线及其以北正午太阳高度夏至日最大、冬至日最小，南回归线及其以南反之；南北回归线之间一年有两次直射，最大值能到 90°。
points: 同一纬度上，正午太阳高度一年里有一个最高值、一个最低值。
在北回归线及其以北的纬度带，夏至日达最大值、冬至日达最小值；在南回归线及其以南的纬度带，情况正好相反。
在南北回归线之间各地，每年受到太阳直射两次，最高值就是 90°；赤道的最低值出现在二至日，是 66°34′。

zh.q: 正午的太阳，什么时候会跑到头顶的北边？
zh.concl: 北回归线以北全年正午太阳在南方，南回归线以南全年在北方；南北回归线之间，一年里正午太阳有时在南、有时在北，直射时正在头顶。
points: 方向由观测点纬度与直射点纬度之差决定：观测点比直射点更北，正午太阳就在南方。
北回归线以北 φ 总是大于 δ，所以全年正午太阳都在南方；南回归线以南反之。
只有在南北回归线之间，δ 会超过 φ，正午太阳的方向才随季节南北翻号。

zh.q: 为什么北半球 6、7、8 月算夏天，南半球却是冬天？
zh.concl: 太阳辐射的年变化形成四季；气候统计上北温带许多国家 3–5 月春、6–8 月夏、9–11 月秋、12–2 月冬，南半球与北半球正好相反。
points: 由于昼夜长短和正午太阳高度的时空变化，太阳辐射在一年中呈现有规律的变化，形成四季。
从天文含义看，夏季是一年内白昼最长、正午太阳高度最高的季节（昼长归 GEO-01，本课只作文字）。
教材在气候统计上把 3、4、5 月划为春季，6、7、8 月划为夏季，9、10、11 月划为秋季，12、1、2 月划为冬季；南半球与北半球正好相反。

zh.q: 热带、温带、寒带的界线，为什么落在两组纬度上？
zh.concl: 以南北回归线和南北极圈为界，地球表面粗略划分为热带、北温带、南温带、北寒带和南寒带；界线纬度是 ±23°26′ 和 ±66°34′。
points: 以南北回归线和南北极圈为界，可以把地球表面粗略地划分为热带、北温带、南温带、北寒带和南寒带。
热带一年有两次直射；温带既没有直射，也没有极昼和极夜；寒带有极昼和极夜。
南北极圈的纬度是 66°34′ = 90° − 23°26′：教材正文没写这个数，它是由黄赤交角推出来的。

zh.q: 考核：按四道题，在球面上点出对应的地方
zh.concl: 直射点在南北回归线之间往返，所以热带一年有两次直射、回归线以外一次也没有；极圈以内有极昼极夜，那里就是寒带。
points: 判断某地属于哪一带，先把它与回归线、极圈的关系摆出来。
一年两次直射（热带）、一次也没有（温带）、有极昼极夜（寒带），正是五带划分的直接后果。
点错不算过：要说清「我点的地方为什么不在此列」。

en.q: Why can the sun only be overhead between the two tropics?
en.concl: Because the obliquity is 23°26′ and the axis keeps its direction while Earth's position in orbit changes, the point where sunlight strikes vertically can only travel between the tropics, as far north as 23°26′N and as far south as 23°26′S.
points: The angle between the equatorial plane and the ecliptic plane is the obliquity of the ecliptic; at present it is 23°26′.
As Earth revolves, the direction of its axis in space and the size of the obliquity can be taken as constant over a given period.
So the sun is overhead as far north as 23°26′N and as far south as 23°26′S; these two limits are the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.

en.q: How does the subsolar point make this trip in a year?
en.concl: The subsolar point travels between the tropics with a period of one year: the annual migration of the subsolar point; this period is a tropical year, and the equinoxes and solstices are the four key dates on the route.
points: Around the June solstice (about 21 June) the sun is overhead at 23°26′N, then the subsolar point gradually moves south.
At the September equinox (about 23 September) it is overhead at the equator, at the December solstice (about 22 December) at 23°26′S, then it gradually returns north.
This back-and-forth movement between the tropics is the annual migration of the subsolar point; one round trip takes a tropical year.

en.q: How high does the sun climb at noon in Beijing on the June solstice?
en.concl: Noon sun altitude a = 90° − |φ − δ|: 90° at the subsolar point, 0° on the terminator, and elsewhere decreasing with the latitude difference from the subsolar point; Beijing 40°N has 73°26′ at the June solstice and 26°34′ at the December solstice.
points: Solar altitude is the angle between the sun's rays and the ground; at the subsolar point the solar altitude is 90°.
The noon sun altitude is the highest solar altitude of the day and reflects the strength of solar radiation.

The noon sun altitude can be calculated as a = 90° − |φ − δ|, with δ positive in the summer half-year and negative in the winter half-year; Beijing (40°N) has 73°26′ at the June solstice and 26°34′ at the December solstice. The angle between the small Beijing plate on the globe and the horizontal rays is a; the magnified view above lays that patch of ground flat, and the number by the arc changes with the date.

en.q: On the same day, why is the sun lower the further north you go?
en.concl: By latitude, the noon sun altitude decreases north and south from the Tropic of Cancer at the June solstice, from the equator at the equinoxes, and from the Tropic of Capricorn at the December solstice.
points: On the same day, the further a latitude is from the subsolar point, the lower the noon sun altitude.
So the highest point of the curve (and of the real Earth) is always on the subsolar latitude, and it moves north and south with the date.
At the June solstice the peak is at the Tropic of Cancer, at the December solstice at the Tropic of Capricorn, and at the equinoxes at the equator.

en.q: When does the local noon sun altitude reach its highest and lowest values?
en.concl: At and north of the Tropic of Cancer the noon sun altitude is highest at the June solstice and lowest at the December solstice, the reverse at and south of the Tropic of Capricorn; between the tropics the sun is overhead twice a year and the maximum reaches 90°.
points: At a given latitude, the noon sun altitude has one highest and one lowest value in the year.
In the belt at and north of the Tropic of Cancer it peaks at the June solstice and is lowest at the December solstice; at and south of the Tropic of Capricorn it is the other way round.
Everywhere between the tropics has the sun overhead twice a year, so the maximum is 90°; at the equator the minimum comes at the solstices and is 66°34′.

en.q: When does the noon sun move to the north side of the zenith?
en.concl: North of the Tropic of Cancer the noon sun is in the south all year, south of the Tropic of Capricorn in the north all year; between the tropics it is sometimes south and sometimes north, and directly overhead when the sun is overhead.
points: The direction depends on the difference between the observer's latitude and the subsolar latitude: if the observer is further north than the subsolar point, the noon sun is in the south.
North of the Tropic of Cancer φ is always greater than δ, so the noon sun is in the south all year; south of the Tropic of Capricorn the reverse.
Only between the tropics can δ exceed φ, so only there does the noon sun switch between north and south with the seasons.

en.q: Why are June, July and August summer in the Northern Hemisphere but winter in the Southern?
en.concl: The annual change in solar radiation creates the seasons; for climate statistics many countries in the north temperate zone take March–May as spring, June–August summer, September–November autumn and December–February winter, and the Southern Hemisphere is exactly the opposite.
points: Because day length and noon sun altitude change over time and place, solar radiation varies regularly through the year, giving the seasons.
In the astronomical sense, summer is the season with the longest days and highest noon sun of the year (day length belongs to GEO-01; here it is text only).

For climate statistics the textbook takes March, April, May as spring, June, July, August as summer, September, October, November as autumn, and December, January, February as winter; the Southern Hemisphere is exactly the opposite.

en.q: Why do the boundaries of the tropical, temperate and frigid zones fall on two pairs of latitudes?
en.concl: Using the tropics and polar circles as boundaries, Earth's surface is roughly divided into tropical, north temperate, south temperate, north frigid and south frigid zones; the boundary latitudes are ±23°26′ and ±66°34′.
points: Using the tropics and polar circles as boundaries, Earth's surface can be roughly divided into the tropical zone, north and south temperate zones, and north and south frigid zones.
The tropical zone has the sun overhead twice a year; the temperate zones have neither an overhead sun nor polar day and night; the frigid zones have polar day and night.
The polar circles are at 66°34′ = 90° − 23°26′: the textbook text doesn't give this number; it is derived from the obliquity.

en.q: Assessment: follow four questions and click the matching places on the globe
en.concl: The subsolar point travels between the tropics, so the tropical zone has the sun overhead twice a year and nowhere outside the tropics has it at all; inside the polar circles there are polar day and night, and that is the frigid zone.
points: To decide which zone a place belongs to, first state its relation to the tropics and polar circles.
Overhead twice a year (tropical), never (temperate), polar day and night (frigid): these are the direct results of the five-zone division.
